A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TableMaster study. Their readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison despite formatting and organizational changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original TableMaster evaluations, reproduced baselines, ablations, and challenge analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds a token-usage experiment in Appendix I.2, Table 9.

M1.justification: Section 4, Algorithm 1, and the method prompts retain the same extraction, reconstruction, verbalization, and adaptive reasoning procedures. The added fallback discussion does not establish a procedural change; full-table fallback was already described in v3 Appendix M.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate WikiTQ, TabFact, FetaQA, HiTab, and FinQA, including the same noisy-table scenarios. The new efficiency experiment uses a subset of the existing TabFact task; the dataset summary adds documentation rather than coverage.

E2.justification: Chain-of-Table becomes an empirical token-usage comparator in v4 Appendix I.2, where v3 only discussed its efficiency qualitatively. Comparator membership in the retained accuracy experiments is unchanged. Newly cited Fortune, TablePilot, and H-STAR are not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added efficiency experiment measures prompt and completion tokens on the first 100 TabFact examples using GPT-4o without self-consistency decoding. This introduces a limited new evaluation protocol; the retained experiments do not establish revised settings or reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 adds a direct analysis of token consumption against Chain-of-Table, supplementing the existing table-area cost and condensation analyses. Component ablations, size sensitivity, noisy-table tests, adaptive-reasoning analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed variation, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across repeated experimental runs. Existing single-inference and self-consistency descriptions are unchanged; the new token comparison adds no uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v4 Table 9 newly reports 3,393.5 prompt and 738.6 completion tokens for TableMaster, versus 13,209.6 and 914.2 for Chain-of-Table. These are new cost results, not improved accuracy under an earlier setting. Matched benchmark scores, ablation values, and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formalization, reconstruction algorithm, notation definitions, and Appendix I.1 cost derivation, including Equation 1, are retained. No mathematical correction, new formal assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the four challenges, unified framework, adaptive reasoning contribution, and headline 78.13% WikiTQ accuracy with GPT-4o-mini. The added aspirational closing sentence in the abstract does not change the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Appendix I.2 newly attributes token savings to early exits and full-table fallbacks, contrasting these with repeated table transformations. Appendix A expands discussion of erroneous symbolic operations and uneven performance across languages, domains, and spreadsheet conventions. Existing technical limitations remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix C and Table 3 provide dataset test counts, table types, domains, licenses, and source links. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated experimental changes. The new WikiTQ count of 4,217 is not reconciled with the retained 4,344-example analyses.

R1.justification: v4 adds Fortune, TablePilot, and H-STAR citations, acknowledging H-STAR as concurrent adaptive-reasoning work. It removes v3 Appendix B's dedicated novelty comparison, including the explicit claim that verbalization for semantic enrichment had not previously been explored. The main research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites the ethics statement, removes the dedicated scope/comparison appendix, moves limitations from C to B, and adds dataset and LLM-use appendices. It also changes citation style and publication headers and trims the ablation summary. Most scientific prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds the dataset-summary and token-usage tables. Conference formatting changes headings, author presentation, table sizing, and placement of existing material. Figures 1–29, including the prompt diagrams, are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly strengthens the paper by adding directly measured token costs where v3 relied on table-area proxies, and by documenting dataset provenance. The gains are limited: the 100-example cost comparison lacks accompanying accuracy, and the new 4,217 WikiTQ test count remains unexplained alongside the retained 4,344-example analyses. The method and original accuracy evidence are unchanged.
